questions.prompt: Which commit made tally.sh accept negative numbers (the first fixed commit)?
Why did one commit on the way have to be skipped?
options: tally.sh had a syntax error there, so the script could not run and the behaviour could not be judged
It was a merge commit, and merges cannot be bisected
Git skips every third commit to save time

goals.label: Let bisect narrow the search down to one commit

check.script: t=$(git rev-parse --git-path BISECT_TERMS); { read -r new; read -r old; } < "$t" 2>/dev/null || { new=bad; old=good; }; b=$(git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/bisect/$new") || exit 1; [ "$(git rev-list --count "$b" --not $(git for-each-ref --format='%(objectname)' "refs/bisect/$old-*"))" = 1 ] && git show "$b:tally.sh" | bash -s -- -2 5 >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! git show "$b^:tally.sh" | bash -s -- -2 5 >/dev/null 2>&1

goals.label: Identify the commit that fixed negative numbers
Finish the search with git bisect reset (no bisect in progress)
